blocks.content:
A person is qualified to be a High Court judge if:
• He or she is a citizen of India
• Has held a judicial office for at least 10 years, OR
• Has been an advocate of a High Court for at least 10 years
A person is qualified to be a High Court judge if:

items: Crucial distinction: The experience requirement is 10 years for both judicial office and advocate practice, connected by an 'OR' condition.
Distinction between Supreme Court and High Court judge qualifications: High Court requires 10 years of judicial office or advocacy experience.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The candidate must hold Indian citizenship as a mandatory prerequisite.
Requires holding a judicial office in India for a minimum period of 10 years.
Alternatively, requires practicing as an advocate of a High Court for at least 10 years.
